title: Tessa closed enums — SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH
description: CONTRACT.md §7.4. These were previously hand-maintained in four places (CONTRACT.md, index.ts, core/*.py, tests) and would have drifted. TypeScript and Python are now GENERATED from this file by build-enums.mjs. Adding a value to any set marked closed:true is a BREAKING change requiring a PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.

meta.naming: camelCase for multi-word values on the wire, matching the existing cloudOnly / cwdChanged / titleChanged. The DB may use snake_case internally (spec §6 calls its trigger_type column 'INTERNAL, richer') — the wire and the schema are not the same thing.

AgentState.description: CONTRACT §4.1 evt.agent.state. Orb drives the sphere from this; Console drives its status bar.

values.note: nothing in flight
capturing audio (Orb)
model call in flight
TTS playing (Orb)
executing tools, making progress unattended

ADDED pre-approval. Waiting on the owner's approval. Distinct from `working`: at 2am you need to tell 'busy' from 'stuck waiting for you' at a glance. Orb renders amber and static; Console shows it in the status bar.
approval outstanding, still live
spec v3.0 called this `done`; renamed to pair with `failed`

ADDED pre-approval. An approval expired unanswered after 30 minutes (spec §5 rule 5). Deliberately not `failed` (nothing broke) and not `cancelled` (nobody cancelled). Distinct from `blocked`: blocked is still waiting, needsReview means the window closed.

CreatedBy.description: CONTRACT §4.1 evt.job.created. What caused this job to exist.

values.note: cron / time trigger
ADDED pre-approval. Phase 5 file-watch trigger.
ADDED pre-approval. Phase 5 inbound mail trigger.
ADDED pre-approval. Phase 5 webhook trigger.

ADDED pre-approval, NOT in the owner's list. Spec §3.4/line 396 lists five trigger types: time, file-watch, email, webhook, AND system event. Omitting it would have forced a version bump the first time a job fires on battery-low, lock, or device-connect — exactly the unattended triggers this agent is for.

PtyReportEvent.description: CONTRACT §6.5 cmd.pty.report. Keeps the audit trail complete even though the daemon never sees the byte stream.

values.note: ADDED pre-approval. Without it, a node-pty spawn failure leaves an issued grant with no terminal event: dangling grant, broken audit trail. With a beta native module and no MSVC on this machine, that is a realistic path, not a theoretical one. The daemon reclaims the grant on receipt.

Surface.description: CONTRACT §2.2 cmd.hello. Deliberately NOT extended with `mobile` — see the rationale in the report and CONTRACT §2.4.

Tier.description: CONTRACT §6.4. Defined once in core/config/permissions.yaml. Unchanged — spec §6 defines exactly three and no fourth is implied through Phase 8.

Provenance.description: CONTRACT §6.2. Where a byte, an action, or a piece of context came from. This is the prompt-injection boundary: everything except `human` is untrusted.

values.note: the owner typed or clicked it — the only trusted source
process stdout/stderr on this machine
model-proposed
an unattended trigger

ADDED pre-approval. Content fetched from off this machine: email bodies, web pages, remote READMEs. §6.1 makes all of it untrusted data, but with only `program` available there was no way to TAG it as such. Phase 3 adds browser and Phase 5 adds mail; without this the provenance chain silently mislabels the highest-risk category.

ADDED pre-approval. The daemon's own actions (daemon.start, auth.lockout). core/security/audit.py already writes actor='system' — this aligns the wire enum with what the audit log has been emitting since commit one.

ADDED pre-approval. Change directory in the focused terminal instead of spawning a new one. This is what VS Code's tree does and the most commonly wanted default in a terminal with a file tree — the owner may well prefer it to a new window after a week of use. Note it must NOT be reachable from a deep link (§6.6), because it mutates an existing session's state.

ADDED pre-approval. A OneDrive file switching between cloud-only and local is not create/modify/delete/rename — the content is unchanged, only its cloud state moved. With 17,340 reparse points and the Hydration Firewall as a headline feature, the tree needs to repaint the cost badge on this event and has no other way to hear about it.

CloudState.description: CONTRACT §4.2 FsEntry.cloudState, derived from attributes alone — never by opening the file.

values.note: ADDED pre-approval. Microsoft documents FILE_ATTRIBUTE_UNPINNED as 'internal use only', and Dropbox/Google Drive use different reparse tags. Without `unknown` the enumerator must guess, and a wrong guess in the Hydration Firewall either blocks a local file or lets a metered download through silently. Failing honestly is the safer default.

Decision.description: CONTRACT §4.1 evt.permission.resolved and §5.1 cmd.permission.respond. NOTE the asymmetry: a surface may only SEND approve|deny. `expired` is daemon-emitted only.

values.note: ADDED pre-approval, and a direct consequence of accepting needsReview. evt.permission.request carries expiresAt; when 30 minutes pass unanswered the daemon must broadcast a resolution so the OTHER surface dismisses its approval card. With only approve|deny it could not, and a stale card would hang on the Orb forever. A surface sending `expired` is a contract violation.

Role.description: CONTRACT §4.1 transcript messages. Unchanged — covers the full tool-use loop through Phase 8.

NotificationLevel.description: CONTRACT §4.1 evt.notification. Unchanged — severity, not category. Job outcomes ride evt.job.completed, not this.

ErrorCode.description: CONTRACT §5.4. DELIBERATELY OPEN — see §7.4. Consumers MUST have a default branch. Diagnostic codes will keep accruing through Phase 8, and making every new one a breaking change would be absurd.

values.note: ADDED. Pairs with Decision.expired.
ADDED. CloseCode 4429 existed with no in-band equivalent for a request refused without closing the socket.
ADDED. Spec §6 mandates a hard nightly budget cap. A job refused on budget is not permission.denied — the owner never denied anything.
ADDED. Spec §3.9 requires graceful degradation when the Claude API is unreachable: queue, don't crash. The surface must be able to tell 'offline' from 'broken'.

CloseCode.description: CONTRACT §2.2. DELIBERATELY OPEN. Standard RFC 6455 codes (1001 going away, 1009 message too big) are used unchanged and are not re-declared here.
